H1.statement: COS + analytic Jacobian + LM (1 core, ~200 options): p99 < 10 ms
H1.measured: p50=2.35 ms, p99=4.51 ms (synthetic Gate G2 p99=8.30 ms)

H2.statement: Grid surrogate + LM (Eigen float32) >= 3x faster than E0 (1 core) with in-domain IV RMSE <= 0.05 vol pts
H2.measured: 64x4 (+COS audit): 5.51x faster (0.426 vs 2.35 ms), in-domain RMSE=0.0420 vp; 128x4 (+COS audit): 4.06x faster (0.579 ms), in-domain RMSE=0.0359 vp

H3.statement: Inverse warm-start reduces LM iterations >= 40% (median) vs cold start
H3.measured: Market proxy E1 (same LM config): 8.0 -> 5.0 iters (37.5% reduction); E5 hybrid (5-iter cap): 5.0 iters; Synthetic Heston test (Gate G5): 8.0 -> 3.0 iters (62.5% reduction)

H4.statement: On SPX/misspecified market, Heston structural error dominates surrogate error by >= 10x (RMSE)
H4.measured: Structural Heston RMSE=0.470 vp vs Surrogate RMSE=0.0176 vp (ratio=26.6x; note: measured on synthetic_bates_spx_proxy)

H5.statement: Pointwise random-grid surrogate (E3) is slower than exact COS (E0) in standard Heston
H5.measured: E3 p50=3.59 ms vs E0 p50=2.35 ms (1.53x slower even with batched Eigen GEMM + reverse-mode Jacobian; Phase 6 synthetic ratio=1.41x)
